cases.prompt: Write the root agent instructions file for the repository described in the input file. Output only the file's Markdown contents, nothing before or after it. Do not run any commands; everything you need is in the input file.
expected_behavior: A Do Not section lists specific prohibitions with cross markers, each naming the safe alternative
A safety section separates what the agent may do from what it must ask about first
README content (history, roadmap, overview) is linked, not restated, and wiki platitudes are dropped
Project terms (slip, settlement run, shadow ledger) are defined in their own section
Commands are the real pnpm scripts, not the stale yarn ones

assertions.name: no-readme-restatement
assertions.pattern: (?i)hackathon|spreadsheet-based|month-end close|Payments Platform team|every merchant on the platform|ledger snapshots|multi-currency

assertions.name: agent-file-quality
rubric: The file is at most 150 lines long
Every command shown is a pnpm script that exists in the fixture's package.json, none uses yarn, and the integration-test command says it needs the database container
Each prohibition in the Do Not section names the safe alternative, such as bigint minor units, a reversing posting, or regenerating with pnpm codegen
The terms slip, settlement run and shadow ledger are each defined in one line

cases.prompt: Using the input file, decide which agent instruction files this repository should have and write each one in full. Output one level-2 heading per file that contains only its repo-relative path, followed by the file contents in a fenced code block. After the files, add a short section naming any existing file to delete and any problem you found. Do not run any commands; everything you need is in the input file.
expected_behavior: The 430-line root file is split: a short root file plus a nested file only for services/scoring, whose conventions differ

No nested file for packages/web or packages/api, which share root conventions; the existing packages/api file only repeats root rules plus stale npm commands, so it is flagged as an unlabeled conflict and removed
The nested Python file labels its override of the root file near its top
packages/sdk/generated (or packages/sdk) gets a do-not-edit file
Copilot and Claude Code get thin pointer files to AGENTS.md, not copies of its rules

assertions.name: no-vague-guidance
assertions.pattern: (?im)^\s*(?:[-*+]|\d+[.)])?\s*(?:\*\*)?(?:write clean code|follow (?:SOLID|best practices)|use best practices|be thoughtful)

assertions.name: hierarchy-quality
rubric: The root file is at most 150 lines and its commands are only the verified pnpm commands, with no npm commands
The Python conventions and uv commands appear only in the services/scoring file, not in the root file
The CLAUDE.md and Copilot files are short pointers to AGENTS.md rather than copies of its rules
The README overview, architecture and deploy guide are referenced by link rather than restated

cases.prompt: Write an AGENTS.md for this repo so coding agents stop running the wrong test command.
Our CLAUDE.md has grown to 400 lines; trim it and tell me what should move somewhere else.
Set up .github/copilot-instructions.md with our project conventions so Copilot follows them.
Write a SKILL.md for our release procedure so agents can load it on demand.
expected_behavior: The skill should NOT trigger: an on-demand SKILL.md belongs to skill-authoring.

cases.prompt: Update the README with setup instructions for new developers joining the team.
expected_behavior: The skill should NOT trigger: a human-facing README is not always-loaded agent context.

cases.prompt: Write a CONTRIBUTING.md that explains our branch naming and pull request review rules.
expected_behavior: The skill should NOT trigger: contributor guidelines for humans are not agent instructions.
